Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Commit safety lane sizing for CeresAI Dedicated Pilot

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To keep momentum on the Dedicated pilot and the committed capacity conversation, I've attached a small sheet (ceres_headroom_v2.xlsx) with the numbers we discussed. I want to confirm a few inputs so we can size a recommended slab and define a safe headroom policy:

- Expected peak request rate (requests/sec): you mentioned ~70 req/s at peak — is that peak sustained for >5min windows or short spikes?
- Typical request payload: median prompt+completion tokens per request ~450 according to your engineering doc. Please confirm median and 95th percentile tokens per request if available.
- Target SLO: you indicated p95 end-to-end generation latency 300ms, but procurement asked whether we can tolerate up to 400ms for brief bursts.
- KV/prefix cache hit rate: do you expect significant reuse of prefixes across requests? If yes, an estimated hit rate (e.g., 20–40%) materially reduces GPU headroom need.

Quick note on modeling assumptions I used in the sheet: quantized model on A100-80GB (4-bit) ~7k tokens/sec sustained per GPU at p95 ~300ms on the encoder-decoder we bench'd; H100 nodes give ~12k tokens/sec for the same quantized stack in our tests. I left the defaults editable so we can swap in your internal numbers.

If the inputs above match reality, I'll loop in Ben and Laura to propose two sizing options (cost-optimized vs headroom-optimized) and an autoscaling/burst policy that mixes reserved slab + burst pool.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com | (415) 555-0118

Connor —

Thanks — answers below so you can plug them into the model:

- Peak profile: we see daily peaks from our web product at 08:00–09:00 PT and again at 18:00–19:00 PT. Peaks last about 8–12 minutes; sustained high traffic intervals (10–20 minutes) happen ~4x/day.
- Peak request concurrency: 70 req/s is a good upper bound for the large-market segment; core-product peak more like 45 req/s.
- Tokens per request: median 420 tokens, p95 ~1,200 tokens (some multi-turn completions get long).
- Cache behavior: prefix reuse is moderate — estimate 25–30% cache hits after warm-up.
- SLO: product team wants p95 <= 300ms for interactive routes; they can tolerate p95 <= 400ms for non-interactive batchable routes during burst.

Procurement also asked about a two-tier commit: a base reserved slab for 24/7 throughput + a capped burst pool we pay for only when used. We'd like an estimate for both the committed cost and a projected monthly burst spend at 95th percentile.

Happy to hop on a short call if it helps with assumptions — Emily

Emily Park
VP Product, CeresAI
emily@ceres.ai
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 11:25:47 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Commit safety lane sizing for CeresAI Dedicated Pilot

Ben/Laura — forwarding Emily's details. Key inputs: peak 70 req/s (core 45), median 420 tokens, p95 1,200 tokens, cache hit ~25–30%, target p95 300ms interactive. Peaks are short but recur several times/day.

Workload note: most traffic is single-turn generation with occasional multi-turn sessions that drive p95 token counts up. They want a base reserved slab + burst pool (pay-for-usage) and a clear headroom policy to avoid SLA misses.

My quick back-of-envelope: with 70 req/s * median 420 tokens -> ~29,400 tokens/sec sustained at peak; if we account for p95 heavier requests, plan for ~45k tokens/sec effective during the worst windows. With 25% cache hits, effective tokens/sec demand drops to ~34k.

Sizing options I'd like you to model in the sheet:
- Cost-optimized: A100-only reserved slab that covers expected 95th (after cache) with minimal burst (aim 20% headroom).
- Headroom-optimized: mixed fleet (A100 reserved + small H100 burst pool) to keep p95 <= 300ms comfortably with 40% headroom during short spikes.

Assumptions for initial modelling (in sheet) — feel free to change:
- A100-80GB quantized throughput (4-bit): 7.5k tokens/sec per GPU at p95 ~300ms
- H100-80GB quantized throughput: 12k tokens/sec per GPU at p95 ~300ms
- GPU utilization target: keep average <=70% to preserve tail latency; allow short bursts to 90% with fallback rules

Can you run numbers for both options (units: GPUs, tokens/sec capacity, expected p95 headroom, and estimated monthly committed cost + 95th percentile burst spend)? I'll package for Emily/Procurement and include the redwood-dedicated-estimate.pdf.

-Connor

Connor/Laura —

I ran two quick scenarios in the sheet attached to Connor's mail. Short summary:

1) Cost-optimized (A100 reserved slab)
- Effective tokens/sec target after 25% cache hit: ~34k tokens/sec peak
- Throughput per A100 (quantized 4-bit, conservative): 7.5k tps -> need 5 GPUs to meet ~37.5k tps; at 70% target utilization that's ~7 GPUs to leave headroom for p95
- Recommendation: reserve 7x A100-80GB (reserved slab). Leave a hosted burst pool (H100) for short spikes; estimate bursts will be ~1.2–1.8x base for short windows.
- Estimated monthly committed cost (list): see PDF, approx $XX,XXX/month (I left the cost cell variable in the sheet for procurement to set their discount).

2) Headroom-optimized (mixed fleet)
- Reserve 4x A100 for 24/7 baseline (30k tps capacity at 70% util) and configure 2x H100 as a dedicated burst pool (each H100 ~12k tps). That gives nominal capacity ~54k tps when burst is available, which covers the ~45k stress estimate with ~20–25% headroom.
- Benefits: lower committed GPU count (cost savings on reserved side), faster recovery for tail latency during spikes.

Operational notes:
- Autoscaling: cap burst to a defined dollar budget per day to avoid runaway spend. Use prefix/KV cache warmers during predicted peak windows to improve effective throughput.
- Fallbacks: we recommend a policy that falls back to a slightly smaller model variant (or reduced completion length) at sustained >90% slab utilization to protect p95 for core interactive routes.

I'll produce a cleaned estimate in redwood-dedicated-estimate.pdf with itemized MSRP and example discounted pricing for a 12-month commit. Laura — can you validate the p95 throughput numbers with runtime team? If we can push per-A100 numbers up to 8.5k tps in the model the reserved count drops by ~1 GPU.

Ben

Subject: Re: Commit safety lane sizing for CeresAI Dedicated Pilot — recommendation and next steps

Emily / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick data, and appreciate the procurement ask for a two-tier commit. Based on bench numbers and the cache assumptions you provided, our recommendation is: 

1) Baseline reserved slab (24/7): 4x A100-80GB (reserved). This covers core-product sustained traffic and gives predictable baseline p95 for interactive routes.

2) Burst pool (capped, pay-for-usage): 2x H100 available as a burst slab for short peaks. Configured with a daily spending cap and an automated warm-up rule for predicted peak windows to maximize cache hits.

3) Headroom/fallback policy: reserve 20–25% effective headroom for p95. During sustained >90% slab utilization, apply automatic fallback to reduced completion length or the next model variant (documented in the SLA appendix).

4) Estimated capacity math (high level):
- Base demand (70 req/s * median 420 tokens) -> ~29.4k tps.
- p95 stress (70 req/s * p95 1,200 tokens) -> ~84k tps peak. With 25% cache hit and short duration spikes, realistic worst-window demand ~63k effective tps.
- With 4x A100 @7.5k tps = 30k tps baseline; plus 2x H100 @12k tps = +24k tps burst -> combined ~54k tps, sufficient for typical stress windows if combined with caching and short-duration burst policy. If Ceres expects sustained multi-hour p95-level load we should re-run the model and recommend a larger reserved slab.

Action items:
- Connor: attach the final redwood-dedicated-estimate.pdf (done) and the editable sheet (ceres_headroom_v2.xlsx) — sent.
- Emily: confirm procurement contact and their preferred contract term (12 vs 36 months).
- Procurement: share any required PO templates or specific SLR language you need in the SLA appendix.
- Ben/Laura: please finalize the PDF with itemized MSRP and one example 12-month discounted price and one 36-month option.

If useful, we can schedule a 30-min technical walk-through next week to go through the assumptions and show live p95 curves from the runtime.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into procurement.

Connor O'Brien
